title: How Do Spiders Spin Webs? 🕸️ Fun Facts for Kids
description:
Spiders make silk inside their bodies! Leo asks, big sister Mia explains how a spider builds its web, step by step, in under a minute.

The CurioKids Club: short, curious answers to kids' big questions. Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@CurioKidsClub

lines.text: Mia, how do spiders spin webs?
Spiders make silk inside their bodies! It comes out of tiny parts at their back end, called spinnerets.
Is the silk wet or dry?
It starts runny inside, but as the spider pulls it out, it turns into a strong, stretchy thread.
How does it start a web between two branches?
Many spiders let out a thread and wait for the breeze to carry it across. When it sticks, that's the first bridge!
Next, it adds a frame, then spokes like a bike wheel, and last, a sticky spiral that goes round and round.
Why doesn't the spider get stuck?
Clever trick! Not all the threads are sticky, and the spider steps carefully, mostly on the non-sticky ones.
It's a trap for flying bugs, like flies. And some spiders even eat their old web to make new silk!
Silk from spinnerets, a bridge, spokes and a sticky spiral. Spiders are smart builders!
They sure are! Ask a grown-up to subscribe to The Curio Kids Club for more wonders! And next time someone asks... how do spiders spin webs?
